items.title: improve the string match itself.
items.creator: andy
items.box:
WHAT IS: probabilityStringMatch(A, B)
- A exactly equal to B: 1.0. Not a string, or one side empty: 0.
- Otherwise the shorter string is graded against the longer, both lowercased and accents folded, as the weighted mean of four signals:
  - match (1.0): whole 1.0, starts with 0.7, found inside 0.35, only some of its words 0.15; no word found at all: 0.
  - coverage (0.2): the shorter's length over the longer's.
  - words (0.3): the share of the shorter's characters found in the longer's words, whole words first, then the best part of a word.
  - order (0.25): the longest run of matched words in the same order.
- Upper and lower case cost nothing: relay against Relay scores 1.0.
- Distance costs nothing: matched words side by side and 498 words apart score alike on every signal but match.

HOW WE MAKE IT BETTER
1. Case counts: 0.000001 is subtracted for every character whose case differs, counted over the characters that matched ignoring case. Relay ranks above relay and reLay for Relay; it orders ties and moves nothing else.
2. Distance counts, and more than order: a fifth signal, proximity = matched words / words spanned from the first match to the last (side by side 1.0). People type words in any order, but words far apart usually belong to different thoughts, so proximity weighs 0.35 and order drops from 0.25 to 0.15. That ratio is a guess.
3. The weights are set by hand for now, and are meant to be learned later from what makes a user happier.

chat.text: what is there right now?

Today: both strings lowercased and accents folded, so case costs nothing (Relay vs relay = 1.0); then 4 weighted signals: exact/starts-with/contains/some-words (1.0), length coverage (0.2), word match (0.3), word order (0.25).
Order counts, distance does not: relay key with 498 words between scores 0.40, side by side at the start 0.71.
Starts-with outweighs length: relay key at the start of 500 words (0.71) beats the relay key answers (0.56).
But "Relay" matches "Relay" better than "relay" matches "Relay", true or false? subtract 0.001 from probability for every character that is a case-missmatch.

True as you mean it, false today: Relay vs Relay and relay vs Relay both score 1.0.
With 0.001 per case-mismatched character, relay vs Relay becomes 0.999, and any other match drops the same way, never below 0.

Se the coal is sequencing the better matches ahead of worse matches, so if we just subtract 0.000001 per mismatched character-case, after 1000 characters with wrong case we still only used 0.001 of the 1.0 budget, but sequencing is achieved.

Agreed: 0.000001 per case-mismatched character only breaks ties, so Relay ranks above relay for Relay and nothing else moves.
The count is over the characters that matched ignoring case (the exact, prefix or found part, and matched words); unmatched characters have no case to compare.
absolutely. any human will tell you that Relay is not exactly the same as relay, or reLay
even visually
Recorded in the box: your Relay question line now reads as the rule, 0.000001 per case-mismatched character; the rest of your draft is untouched.
Yes: the case penalty orders what the eye sees as closer first.
and distance between matching tokens is definitely an indicator of a worse match.

Agreed, and today nothing measures it. Proposal: a proximity signal = matched words / words spanned from the first match to the last, so side by side is 1.0 and relay ... 498 words ... key is 2/500.
Should it weigh like word order (0.25), a real signal rather than a tie-breaker?
it should have mabe the same weight as word order... hard to say: i didn't think it through yet. this is where i'd have a machine learn what makes a user happier......
Recorded in the box: proximity weighted like word order (0.25) for now, the weights to be learned later from what makes a user happier.

agreed.

can you replace the text in the box with a concise summary of what is, and how we make it better?
The box now holds the summary: what the match does today, then the three changes (case, distance, weights learned later).
honest answer please. is distance more important than sequence? your guess? (i have a guess now)

My guess: distance matters more. People type words in any order (key relay for relay key), but two words 500 apart usually belong to different thoughts.
In short labels both barely matter; in long text distance separates a hit from a coincidence.
agreed. pub in box like that with a guessed weight ratio for now, and saying it is a guess.
In the box: proximity 0.35, order down to 0.15, marked as a guess.
green?
Green: settled, open none, box current (v7); the weights stand as a marked guess.

items.title: infrastructure for making searches and lists easy.
items.creator: andy

items.title: shell element list-search-container.
items.creator: andy
items.box:
A shell element: a list with its search, looking the same everywhere it is used.

LAYOUT
[set of filters: icons, or word + icon, checked]
[search string input, its clear button inside it on the right] [search button]
[count line]
[list]

CONFIGURATION (what each use sets): one plain object given at creation, callbacks in it, no registry. The shape:

shellCreateListSearch(container, {
  server: 'deskVerify',                 // the server searched (its stream too)
  verb: 'fallout.reds',                 // the search verb invoked
  args: function (text, filters) {},    // the verb's arguments from the words and the filter values
  filters: [{                           // declared, drawn by the container, the same everywhere
    name: 'outcome',
    choices: [{ value: 'red', icon: '❌', word: 'fail' }, { value: 'green', icon: '✅', word: 'success' }, { value: '', word: 'both' }],
    test: function (row, value) {}      // a probability, 0 to 1: 0 leaves the row out, 1 keeps it as it is, between lowers it; never raises it
  }],
  paint: function (row) {},             // one row's html
  press: function (row) {},             // a press on a row (Fallout: its history dialog)
  empty: 'No test matches.'             // the empty-list sentence
})

A row is the object an answer item's label carries; paint, press and test all take that same object. The words are matched against the whole row (probabilityStringObjectMatch), so nothing configures which text is searched.

WHERE IT LIVES
shell/shared/js/listSearch.js, loaded by an app on demand, as deskElement.js is.

WHAT EVERY SEARCH IT CALLS ANSWERS
{items: [{key, label}], more, total}: key is the identity of what the row shows (one per test, per peer, per item), label the row as json, more true when the answer was capped, total how many matched in all. deskVerify is brought to this in G29.5.

BEHAVIOUR (the same for every use)
- The bucket knows nothing of string matching; the container scores every cached row with probabilityStringObjectMatch per keystroke multiplied by every filter's test, and hands the numbers to bucket.sort. A filter only lowers: the words decide the order among the rows the filters let through.
- Rows are keyed by the key the search answer carries; that key is the identity of what the row shows, so a row a later search brings again replaces the older one.
- Every row any search brought is kept in a cache, a probabilityBucket, unbounded.
- Each character typed or erased redraws the list from the cache at once, ranked by probabilityStringMatch: best matches on top, every row the filters let through shown.
- The server calls MUST be serialized: at most one request of the element on the wire at a time, every verb it calls included. No typing pause: each character typed or erased asks the server at once when nothing is on the wire; while a request is out, the latest words go the moment its answer returns. The round trip paces the server, the cache paces the screen.
- The count line says how many match, and that the answer was partial when the server capped it.

chat.text:
I'm continuing with this one. it might eliminate the remaining item.

in the shell, a list with a search combined should look as similar as possible every where,

[set of filters] [ideally]  [icons] or [word+icon-checked]
[sear string input] [search-button]
[list]

it must configure the server-search-path and/or verb (which server search is invoked)
it must configure a row-painter

what else?

From Fallout: a row key (so a row a later search brings replaces the old) and the row text matched locally; a cache (the bucket) redrawn per keystroke, the server asked when typing pauses, one request on the wire.
The filters mapped to the verb's args; a count line (matched of total, partial when the answer was capped); an empty-list sentence.
A row press handler (Fallout opens its history dialog), and the stream it subscribes to so changed rows repaint themselves.
i see, we must configure the unique row identifier in the database or json table.....?

Not configured in the container if every search answer already carries it: each item is {key, label}, and the key can be the row's identity.
Today it is not everywhere: deskVerify sends its database row number, one per record, while a test's identity is its file plus its key; the desk sends the item id, which is right.
Proposal: a search's key is the identity of what the row shows, so the container keys its cache by it and configures nothing.
Arranged: the box holds the layout, then CONFIGURATION (what each use sets), then BEHAVIOUR (the same for every use).
then we decide if our configuration requirements can support the desired behavior

Missing in configuration: how each filter tests a cached row, since the cache is redrawn locally per keystroke (Fallout tests red or green).
Covered without config: the text matched locally can be the whole row through probabilityStringObjectMatch, which exists.
Not configurable, a rule for every server search: answer {items: [{key = identity, label}], more, total}; deskVerify keys by record today, and stream rows must carry the same key and shape.
add to the behavior the the server calls MUST be serialized, this is VERY important.
In BEHAVIOUR: the server calls MUST be serialized, one request of the element on the wire at a time, every verb included.

if deskAgentRemote searches via a public relay, the response time is MUCH longer than a search on the local node, so every round-trip must block a new search call, so the user may type 6 characters before the next search goes to a server, but the cached/displayed list can be updated with every key stroke.

Agreed, and that is the serialized behaviour in the box: the round trip paces the server, the cache paces the screen.
It makes the typing pause unneeded: send at once when nothing is out, else the latest words go when the answer returns. Drop the pause?
no pause in typing, that's extremely irritating.
In the box: no typing pause; the server is asked at once when nothing is out, else with the latest words when the answer returns.
so this container obiously container a set of probability objects, to we configure filters, filter rendering , row rendering with callbacks or registered function that need a specific format?

Callbacks in one plain object given at creation, no registry: createListSearch(el, {verb, server, args(text, filters), filters, paint(row), press(row), empty}).
Filters are declared, not painted by the app: [{name, choices: [{value, icon, word}], test(row, value)}], and the container draws them, so they look the same everywhere.
A row is the object the answer label carries; paint, press and test all take that same object.

right, good pattern, an object, i agree.

please put a proposed shape for 

shellCreateProbabilityBucket({
foo1(args1),
etc...
})

or something like that?

Proposed shape is in the box under CONFIGURATION: shellCreateListSearch(container, {server, verb, args, filters, paint, press, empty}), filters declared with a test per row.
The name is a proposal: it is a list with its search, the bucket being one of its insides.
Ah so the shellProbabilityBucket knows nothing about stringMatching either?

Right: the bucket stays blind, it only seats and sorts by the numbers it is handed (sort(compare)).
The list-search container does the matching: per keystroke it calls bucket.sort(row => probabilityStringObjectMatch(words, row)), so the app configures no matching either.

cool. i like it.

BTW: one of my favorite things about the test search is: how the search-clear icon-button is on the right inside of the search string box.... very modern!
In the box: the clear button inside the search box on the right, the shape as agreed, and the container (not the bucket) doing the matching.
so i assume that the test:function() returns a probability?

I had it as yes/no; a probability is better and now in the box: 0 leaves the row out, 1 keeps it as is, between lowers it.
A row's score is its string match times every filter's test, one number for the bucket to sort by.
so filter can modify the probability any-which-way, from 0.0 all the way to 1.0 ?

Down only, as written: it multiplies, so a filter can drop a row to 0 or keep it, never lift a 0.4 match above a 0.9 one.
Lifting would need test(row, value, p) returning the new probability; I would keep down-only, so the words always decide the order among what the filters let through.
understood. i agree.
In the box: a filter only lowers, never raises; the words decide the order among what the filters let through.
still good to go on this?

Yes, after two lines into the box: every server search the container calls answers {items: [{key = the identity of the row, label}], more, total} (deskVerify's change to that is G29.5's).
The element lives in shell/shared/js/listSearch.js, loaded by an app on demand as deskElement.js is. Shall I write both in?
tell me when you're done fixing boxes
Done fixing the box: WHERE IT LIVES and WHAT EVERY SEARCH IT CALLS ANSWERS are in; G29.4 is ready for its Go.

items.title: update "Fallout-search" using our new list search element
items.creator: andy
items.box:
PRELIMINARY DRAFT, to refine.

The Fallout pane's Reds list is built with shellCreateListSearch (G29.4), and its own search machinery is deleted.
- Configuration: server deskVerify through the plugin verb fallout.reds; args from the words and the ✅/❌ filter; one filter, outcome (❌ fail, ✅ success, both), whose test passes a row whose outcome matches; paint draws test file | what is tested | status | since; press opens shell/falloutHistory for that test; empty says no test matches.
- deskVerify's search keys each answer row by the test's identity (its file and its key), not its database record, and answers more and total.
- Deleted from the pane: its own cache, its wire slot, its typing timer and its local ranking; a test shows they are gone.
- Unchanged: the summary line (how many red of how many tests now), the history dialog, the Items tab and the goal chat.

items.title: update peer search box, for use in contacts, chatter etc.
items.creator: andy
items.box:
PRELIMINARY DRAFT, to refine.

The peer search box (Contacts' search of the book and of the network, and any other place a peer is picked, chatter included) is built with shellCreateListSearch (G29.4).
- Configuration: the server and verb behind contact.search; a row is a peer, {publicKey, label}, keyed by its public key; paint draws the peer; press does what the using app asks (add to the book, open a chat).
- The ranking moves to the probability modules: peerSearch.js, gradedSearch.js, bucket.js and searchBucket.js are retired wherever the probability modules and the container replace them (hub.js and relay.js rank peers with them today), each removal with a test that it is gone.
- Open: whether hub and relay move in this item or a later one, since they are core.
